resources.string: Closes Instagram Reels. Works only in Instagram.

Reel Block closes the Instagram Reels screen when it opens, by pressing Back for you. To notice Reels, it checks the name of the Instagram screen that is open. It works only in Instagram. It never reads your messages, posts, photos or passwords. It keeps only a count of closed Reels on this phone. It has no internet permission, so nothing leaves your phone, and it keeps no logs.
Reel Block closes the Reels screen as soon as it opens. Your feed, Stories and messages keep working.
No account, no ads, no tracking
To notice when Reels opens, Reel Block needs an Android permission called accessibility. Here is exactly how it uses it.
See the name of the Instagram screen that is open, like the Reels screen
Press Back for you when that screen is Reels
Check which Instagram version is installed, to notice when an update breaks Reel Block
It keeps, only on this phone
How many Reels it closed each day, for 30 days, and in total
Your pause setting, and that you agreed to this page
Reads your messages, posts, photos or passwords
Looks at any app other than Instagram
Uses the internet. It has no internet permission, so nothing can leave your phone
Android will warn you that this kind of app can see your screen. The warning is the same for every app of this kind. The code that keeps these promises is public.
Android opens its Accessibility settings. It takes about 20 seconds.
Find Reel Block. It can be under Downloaded apps or Installed apps.
Turn it on, then tap Allow.
Come back to Reel Block. It shows “Reels are blocked”.
Is the switch grey, or does it say “Restricted setting”?
Android does this for apps that don’t come from an app store. Open App info, tap ⋮ at the top, then Allow restricted settings. Then try again.
Instagram is not on this phone yet. When you install it, Reels will close.
When Reels opens in Instagram, Reel Block takes you back. Everything else works as usual.
Reels open as normal until %1$s. Then blocking turns back on by itself.
Reels open as normal until you turn blocking back on.
Turn it on once in Android settings. Then it works in the background.
Settings still show it as on, but it isn’t running. This can happen when you clear recent apps or when battery saving is strict. Turn Reel Block off and on again.
Instagram %1$s no longer has the Reels screen that Reel Block looks for, so Reels may stay open. Get the newest Reel Block, or let us know.
Open Instagram and tap Reels to try it. The count stays on this phone.
Running. Instagram %1$s has the Reels screen.
Off. Turn it on to start.
Reels screen not found in Instagram %1$s.
Running. Could not read Instagram %1$s right now. Try again later.
Pause or resume from the top of your screen
Swipe down twice from the top of the screen. Tap the pencil, then drag Reel Block into your tiles.
The tile is already in your Quick Settings.
Turn on Autostart, so this phone restarts Reel Block after you clear recent apps
What it can do, what it keeps, and what it never does
Reel Block has no internet permission. It can’t send anything.
It checks screen names. It never reads your messages, posts or photos.
The count stays on this phone and is left out of backups.
